questions.q: Every Azure alert rule is built from which two halves?
options: A severity level and a time zone
A condition (what to watch for) and an action (what happens when it's true)
A metric and a log, with no other components
A resource group and a subscription
questions.explain: An alert rule watches on your behalf and does something the moment its condition is met — the condition and the action are its two core halves.

questions.q: In the condition "CPU > 80% for 5 minutes," why does the 5-minute window matter?
options: It determines which Action Group gets attached
It is required by Azure for all alert rules regardless of signal
It prevents a brief, normal CPU spike from firing a noisy, unhelpful alert
It sets the severity level of the alert automatically
questions.explain: Without an evaluation window, a single 2-second CPU spike that's completely normal would trigger the alert.

options: A reusable, separate object defining what happens when an alert fires — email, SMS, webhook, function, or runbook
A feature exclusive to Log Analytics workspaces
A collection of resource groups being monitored together
A built-in severity rating from Sev 0 to Sev 4
questions.explain: Action Groups are defined once and attached to as many alert rules as needed, so the same notification behavior applies everywhere.

questions.q: What are the four parts of a complete alert rule?
options: Scope, condition, Action Group, and severity
Caller, operation, timestamp, and result
Metric, log, dashboard, and budget
Resource group, subscription, tenant, and region
questions.explain: Scope defines what's watched, the condition defines when it fires, the Action Group defines what happens, and severity helps triage.

questions.q: Why is an Action Group built as its own separate, reusable object instead of being configured individually inside every alert rule?
options: Because Azure alert rules cannot contain any actions directly under any circumstances
Because severity levels require a separate object to function
Because Action Groups are only usable with budget alerts
So the same notification behavior (email, webhook, function, etc.) can be attached to many different alert rules without rebuilding it each time
questions.explain: One Action Group can be attached to a CPU alert, a disk-space alert, and a budget alert alike, so the whole team is notified consistently.
